## Natural history notes

A small tree-climbing songbird characterized by blue-gray upperparts, a white face and breast, black cap, short tail, and a long straight bill. In Florida, the White-breasted Nuthatch is found mainly in mature pine-oak woods, hardwood forests, hammocks, wooded parks, and older neighborhoods with large trees, especially in northern and central parts of the state. It forages by creeping headfirst down trunks and branches, probing bark crevices for insects, spiders, seeds, and nuts, and nests in tree cavities or nest boxes.
